samples.summary: Failover on a child-reported 401/403 lets one session pull the whole credential pool, defeating the one-credential-per-child bound in `credentialEnv`
samples.evidence: `nextCredential` now returns the next pool token whenever `isCredentialRejected(err)` is true (ask.mjs:639), and `isCredentialRejected` (ask.mjs:600-605) is decided from `err.code`/`err.status`, which `classifyResult` copies verbatim from the SDK `result` message (`m.api_error_status`, ask.mjs:380). That message is produced by the `claude` CLI subprocess, which runs with `cwd` set to the UNTRUSTED branch checkout. `credentialEnv` (ask.mjs:548-552) deliberately deletes the other eight pool variables so that a compromised child holds exactly one secret — the mitigation docs/design/harness-engineering.md:1929-1939 records as the pool's residual risk. The new rule undoes that bound: a child that emits `{is_error:true, api_error_status:401}` causes the parent's `for(;;)` loop (ask.mjs:708-721) to immediately spawn a fresh child in the same untrusted cwd holding the NEXT credential, and repeating it walks all nine — the test at ask.test.mjs:292 pins exactly this walk-the-whole-pool behaviour as intended. A weaker form of this vector already existed via `isAccountLimit`'s prose fallback, but it required the child to fake limit prose; a bare status field now suffices, and the widened `SESSION_LIMIT_RE` (redact.mjs:305) adds three more prose triggers. Attacker path: any SDK/CLI compromise or sandbox escape from the untrusted checkout that can shape one result message escalates from stealing 1 token to harvesting the entire pool in one job. The pool is module-scoped (ask.mjs:614-618), so the walk is shared by every lens in the process.

samples.summary: auth-smoke hands EVERY pool credential to each probe subprocess instead of using `credentialEnv`
samples.evidence: `checkCredential` builds the child environment as `{ ...process.env, CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN: authToken }` (auth-smoke.mjs:149), a plain spread that leaves `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN_1..8` in the child. ask.mjs:548-552 exists precisely so this never happens ("a plain spread would hand that child all nine, which is the blast radius harness-engineering.md records as the pool's residual risk") and its docblock claims "one builder ... so the two can never disagree" — but auth-smoke does not call it. This file is touched by the change (it now imports from redact.mjs) and it iterates every slot serially (auth-smoke.mjs:209-216), so each of N probe subprocesses sees all N secrets. Mitigating factors: `allowedTools: []`, `settingSources: []`, and cwd is not forced to the checkout — hence minor rather than major — but it is the same defence-in-depth gap the pipeline explicitly closed elsewhere.

samples.summary: Threat-model section still describes the pre-change failover rule, and its proposed mitigation is invalidated by this change
samples.evidence: harness-engineering.md:1923-1927 states the pool "replaces it only when that account's window closes", which this change makes false — a slot is now retired on 401/403 as well (ask.mjs:639). More importantly the residual-risk bullet's stated remedy, "hand the untrusted-cwd step only the two credentials a round can use (the selected one and its failover)" (harness-engineering.md:1936-1939), no longer bounds anything: a round can now legitimately consume every slot in the pool (ask.test.mjs:292 asserts the full walk). The security invariant an adopter reads before arming the pipeline is therefore stale in the permissive direction, and the recorded mitigation plan would under-provision without being obviously wrong to a future implementer.
searchedFor: grep for `residual risk|blast radius|one credential|pool` in docs/design/harness-engineering.md

samples.summary: Widened QUOTA pattern in the pre-arm check can mask a rejected credential as "nothing is misconfigured"
samples.evidence: `classifyFailure` tests QUOTA before AUTH (auth-smoke.mjs:84-85), and QUOTA now contains the widened `SESSION_LIMIT_RE` (`session|usage|weekly|daily|monthly` + ` limit`, redact.mjs:305) instead of the two narrow literals. Any refusal whose text mentions a billing period alongside a credential problem — e.g. an account-suspension or token-scope message that names a daily/monthly limit — is now reported as `EXIT.quota` with the text "Authentication SUCCEEDED ... Nothing is misconfigured" (auth-smoke.mjs:100-107), and `worstExit` (auth-smoke.mjs:179-183) only escalates to exit 1 if some OTHER slot classified as auth. An expired or revoked secret can therefore leave the pre-arm gate green-ish (exit 2 = "retry later") rather than pointing at the credential, which is the misdiagnosis the file's own header calls the worst thing a pre-arm check can do. I could not produce a real upstream message that hits this, hence low confidence.

verdict.reason: Every claimed location checks out in the working tree. isCredentialRejected (ask.mjs:600-605) accepts err.code === "AUTH_REJECTED" or a bare status of 401/403, and classifyResult derives both from m.api_error_status, a field of the SDK result message emitted by the claude CLI child (ask.mjs:378-386, redact.mjs:400). nextCredential (ask.mjs:638-642) now advances the module-scoped pool (ask.mjs:614-618, token-pool.mjs:169-181) on that signal, and askStructured's for(;;) loop immediately respawns a session with env = credentialEnv(next) (ask.mjs:717-720) in the same untrusted cwd (ask.mjs:476, review-panel.mjs:1484 "every lens runs with cwd: repo on the UNTRUSTED branch checkout"). credentialEnv (ask.mjs:548-552, token-pool.mjs:36-38) exists precisely to bound a child to one secret, and ask.test.mjs:292-302 pins the walk-the-whole-pool behaviour. No guard blocks it: advance's deadToken check (token-pool.mjs:171) only dedupes concurrent reports of the same token and is inert against a sequential walk; tools/dontAsk/settingSources:[] (ask.mjs:501-517) raise the attacker bar to an SDK/CLI-level compromise but do not make the path unreachable, and docs/design/harness-engineering.md:1933-1936 explicitly calls those "defence in depth, not a substitute for the count". Refuting on "a weaker variant already existed via isAccountLimit's 429+prose path" would be judging whether the change introduced the code, which is out of my remit, and credential blast-radius is squarely in the security lane where major is blocking (harness-engineering.md:1273).
